images.caption: Figure 1: Process and performance comparison of three RAG paradigms. NaiveRAG retrieves top-k chunks via dense vector similarity, offering good scalability, high speed, and low cost, but precision is limited by shallow semantic matching. GraphRAG extracts triples and builds a knowledge graph offline using an LLM; it enhances evidence organization capability, but incurs high construction cost and is difficult to update incrementally. SAG extracts events and entities with an LLM and activates dynamic hyperedge structures at query time via SQL; it balances retrieval quality, structural capability, and system overhead, while naturally supporting append-only incremental updates.
